_comment: D1 falsifier re-score + post-D1 mutations (PLAN-01 chunk 7 / D1c). The same 18-row D0 table (mutations-c00697f.json, byte-identical) re-probed on the same pinned tree with a binary built from the D1c tip, plus 3 new rows that target shapes which only exist post-D1 (mutations-d1-df865c7.json). Re-score of the original 18: 9/16 → 9/16 — zero transitions, zero regressions, and the same single tier finding (finance-invert-trustee expected T2, caught by T1 — pre-existing, unchanged). D1's movement is tier crossings in the census, not new falsifiable shapes on these 18 rows: the MISSED rows are the payload trio (D4 owns T3), login-drop-disabled (the app has no always-disabled control), login-signin-ternary-swap (pending-state copy — D3) and finance-variant-class (variant classes are not asserted). New rows: bell-drop-read-all-fetch CAUGHT at T2, matched, by the four click-fetch tests D1b item 3 emits — the first new falsifier this table has gained; polls-new-drop-guard-dep MISSED — every one of the pinned tree's 10 multi-dep OR guards is refused by name (no per-dep legs exist on this tree), so deleting an operand from a refused guard changes nothing the frozen suite asserts; button-rename-capcut-variant MISSED — the cap-cut option is named in a skip title (disclosure, exactly as item 6 ships it) but a named skip is not a test. Rate with the new rows: 10/19. Two independent probe runs (the 18-row table, then the 21-row table, each generating its suite once) produced byte-equal results for the shared 18 rows.

rescoreOfD0Rows.transitions: none — identical status, catching spec, catching test and tier on all 18 rows vs falsifiers-c00697f.json
